_comment: ADOPT: the model inventory the harness runs on (HG-0006). One entry per model ROLE. model_id and prompt_version MUST be pinned (no 'latest'/floating tags). Per the model-risk-operating-model-runbook §2.2 matrix, medium AND high tiers need a passing eval run against THIS pin plus an independent validation sign-off (low is optional). Each eval must identify its dataset, runner and timestamp, and cite its REPORT artifact by ref + sha256 (1.10: a declared pass is not evidence). Verified by scripts/model-provenance-check.mjs, which also re-hashes the report. Replace these demo values with your real models; keep the shape.
_domains_comment: ADOPT (optional, 2.1): `domains` and `domain_validations` cover a model whose OUTPUT carries significance in a specialist domain — shariah, medical, privacy. Model risk asks whether the model is accurate, stable and monitored; it never asks whether the thing the model produced is admissible in that domain, and a statistically excellent model can be confidently wrong in a way only a domain authority sees. So a model may declare `domains: ["<domain>"]` plus one signature per domain in `domain_validations: {"<domain>": "<identity id>"}`. The identity must resolve in docs/governance/identities.json, be a human (an agent validates nothing), sit outside `builders`, and hold the role `<domain>-model-validator` — the role name is DERIVED from the domain, so a new domain needs a new registry identity and no code change. This is an ADDITIONAL signature, never a role swap: `validated_by` still has to be a second-line model-validator, and one person covers both only by holding BOTH roles. Omit both fields entirely and nothing here applies — the check is strictly additive and silent for a manifest that declares no domain. Note what the gate proves: WHO signed, and that they signed against the pin that ships. Whether the determination is SOUND is not a property of a JSON record and is not claimed — that belongs to the accountable body (for Shari'ah, the ISSC; scholars decide permissibility, not this harness). Where a compiled control plan requires a domain capability (e.g. `shariah_model_validation` from profiles/products/shariah-model.json) and no model here names that domain, the gate fails and names the change.

domains: ADOPT: name each domain whose competence this model's output requires — e.g. shariah, medical, privacy — or delete both `domains` and `domain_validations`. An untouched ADOPT row is not a declaration and the gate skips it.

domain_validations.ADOPT: <domain>: ADOPT: the identity id of the human holding <domain>-model-validator in docs/governance/identities.json — a second, distinct signature from validated_by unless one person holds both roles

runtime.suspension: Suspend to manual underwriting if override rate > 15% over 2 weeks or a drift alarm fires; the model-risk function holds the switch.
runtime.fallback: On model or provider outage: route to the manual underwriting queue; no automated limit decisions while degraded.
runtime._fallback_note: ADOPT: the fallback for a domain-significant model — a compliance or structure SCREENING model above all — must FAIL CLOSED into a human queue. 'On outage, let it through' books an approval that no determination ever produced, which is the same defect as a data field whose default asserts a compliance flag nobody set (the UAE Open Finance v2.1 IsShariaCompliant default is exactly that shape: absence reading as an answer). Rebuilding it in your own runtime is worse, because here the absence is silent and the record still looks screened. Queue for human review; never auto-approve. Note also what this file is: a DECLARATION the gate reads. Nothing in the harness observes what the fallback does in production — that evidence comes from your monitoring, not from here.
